706870.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *dʰǵʰúHs (“fish”), but the initial ἰ- (i-) is unetymological and problematic. Compare Old Armenian ձուկն (jukn) and Lithuanian žuvi̇̀s.

706846.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hístāmi, from Proto-Indo-European *stísteh₂ti, the reduplicated present of *steh₂-.

706849.t: From ἱστορέω (hĭstoréō, “to inquire”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā), from ἵστωρ (hístōr, “one who knows, wise one”).

706832.t: From ἶσος (îsos), itself from earlier *ϝῖσϝος (*wîswos), of disputed origin: * The Cretan and Arcadocypriot forms suggest Proto-Hellenic *wíswos, perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *wi- (“to separate”).

706873.t: Uncertain. Beekes states a formation in *-nos- like ἔρνος (érnos), κτῆνος (ktênos).

706866.t: From Proto-Hellenic [Term?], from Proto-Indo-European *wéh₁itis (“twining object”), with remodeling of the suffix like in other tree names (compare ἀκτέα (aktéā, “elder (tree)”) and πτελέα (pteléā, “elm”)).

706853.t: No etymology. Furnée connects the word with ἰξύς (ixū́s, “loins”) assuming a common Pre-Greek origin.

706850.t: Related to ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“to stand”).

706858.t: Disputed. Dialectal variants point to Proto-Hellenic *wiskʰū́s, but since the Mycenaean Greek cognate 𐀂𐀱𐀓𐀺𐀈𐀵 (i-su-ku-wo-do-to) lacks the initial /w/, it may have arisen by analogy with *ϝίς (*wī́s, “power”) (> ἴς (ī́s)).

706864.t: Traditionally derived from εἶμι (eîmĭ, “to be going to go”), which is from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ey-, though most other oxytones in -αμός (-ămós) are substantives (such as ποταμός (potămós)); Beekes suggests it comes from the Attic popular language.

706825.t: From ἰσο- (iso-, “equal, equivalent”) + δύναμις (dŭ́nămĭs, “force, power, strength, authority, value, meaning”) + -ος (-os, suffix forming second-declension compound adjectives).
